summary: The original specification of the File Transfer Protocol (FTP) for moving files between hosts on the ARPANET, written by Abhay Bhushan. Its aims were to promote file sharing, encourage indirect use of remote computers, shield users from differences in file storage, and transfer data reliably. It is designed mainly for use by programs but can be used from a terminal. It was replaced by RFC 542.

eli5.summary: A set of rules that lets one computer hand a file to another computer, even if the two store files differently, so people can share their work.

subtitle: The original ARPANET specification for moving files between hosts using a command channel and separate data connections.

tldr.problem: ARPANET hosts stored files in very different ways, and users and programs needed a common way to share files and use remote storage.
tldr.mechanism: A user opens TELNET connections to a server and sends ASCII commands such as RETR and STOR. The server then opens a separate data connection, with an agreed byte size, type and mode, to carry the file.
tldr.outcome: RFC 354 was replaced by RFC 542 and updated by later RFCs, so it is an early stage of FTP rather than the final design.

facts.label: Text mode EOR and EOF codes

sections.title: Goals and the FTP Model
sections.content:
The File Transfer Protocol (FTP) moves files between hosts on the ARPANET. Its objectives are to promote sharing of files, to encourage indirect use of remote computers by programs, to shield users from differences in file storage systems, and to transfer data reliably and efficiently. It is usable from a terminal but designed mainly for programs.

In the model, the user's TELNET process opens TELNET connections to the server. FTP commands travel to the server over those connections, in ASCII following NVT conventions, and replies come back the same way. The commands set the parameters of a separate data connection: data socket, byte size, transfer mode and representation type. The TELNET connections must stay open while data is being transferred.
sections.eli5: FTP's goal is to let computers share files even when each one keeps its files in its own odd way.

sections.title: The Data Connection, Types and Modes
sections.content:
The user site listens on a data socket. When the server gets a store or retrieve request, the server opens the data connection to that socket. The default byte size is 8 bits, and servers are recommended to implement at least 8 bits. The server also sends a reply naming its own socket so the user can check the connection.

Five representation types are defined: ASCII, Image, Local Byte, Print File-ASCII and EBCDIC Print File. ASCII is the default and needs 8-bit bytes. Four transfer modes are defined: Stream, Text, Block and Hasp, with Stream as the default. In Stream mode, closing the data connection signals end of file. In Block mode each block has a header with a 16-bit byte count and an 8-bit descriptor code.
sections.eli5: The file travels on its own line. The sender can pack the file in different ways, such as plain text or exact bits, as long as both ends agree.

sections.title: Commands and Replies
sections.content:
Commands are ASCII ending in CRLF, with command codes of four or fewer characters. Access control uses USER and PASS. Transfer parameters use BYTE, SOCK, TYPE, STRU and MODE. Service requests include RETR, STOR, APPE, RNFR, DELE, LIST, ALLO, REST, STAT, ABOR and BYE.

Replies are a three digit code, a space and text. The first digit gives the kind of response: 2xx is positive acknowledgment, 3xx means incomplete information, 4xx means an unsuccessful request and 5xx means an incorrect or illegal command. The codes are for programs and the text is for people.
sections.eli5: The user sends short typed orders like "get this file", and the server answers with a number for the computer and a sentence for the human.

sections.title: Error Recovery and Restart
sections.content:
The protocol has no provision for detecting bits lost or scrambled in transfer, saying this is best handled at the NCP level. It does provide a restart procedure for system failures such as a host, an FTP process or the IMP subnet failing.

Restart works only in Block mode. The sender inserts marker blocks into the data stream, and the receiver notes the matching position. After a failure the user sends REST with the marker, followed by the command that was running.
sections.eli5: It is like leaving bookmarks in a long delivery, so if the truck breaks down you resume from the last bookmark.
